applicableAreas: Utility plan showing meter vault near proposed water service tap
findings.comment: Utility plan shows a fire demand meter vault near the water service entrance but does not label the vertical clearance from the top of the vault structure to the sag of the lowest overhead power line. Written clearance approval from Austin Energy is not referenced in the project file.

applicableAreas: Entire site; demolition and construction operations adjacent to transmission structures
findings.comment: Site Demolition Notes on Sheet 8 do not address four required safety clearances for demolition near transmission lines per UCM 1.14.9: (1) pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy at least 48 hours before commencement, (2) barricades erected 10 feet from all transmission structures including guys and anchors within construction area, (3) warning signs placed under overhead electric transmission facilities, and (4) prohibition on materials or spoils storage within the transmission easement.

applicableAreas: Entire site; demolition operations in proximity to at-grade utility appurtenances
findings.comment: Demolition plan does not include a note requiring contractor to use extreme caution when working near at-grade utility appurtenances such as poles, meters, cleanouts, and valve boxes.

applicableAreas: All utility crossing locations and clearance zones throughout site
findings.comment: While utility notes require contractor field verification of existing utility locations prior to construction, the plans do not include an explicit requirement for field verification of all proposed utility separations and clearances (both horizontal and vertical) during construction and prior to final acceptance of the project.

applicableAreas: Staging and storage area located on western portion of site (shown on Sheet 5)
findings.comment: A staging and storage area is delineated on the Erosion Control Plan (Sheet 5), and the biofiltration-detention pond has a water quality volume of 6,388 cubic feet, exceeding the 5,000 cubic feet threshold that triggers the SCM staging area clearance requirement. However, the plans do not demonstrate a labeled 14-foot minimum vertical clearance from the staging area to any existing or proposed vegetation or other objects above the area, including tree canopy at maturity.

applicableAreas: Biofiltration-detention pond and all access points serving the stormwater control measure
findings.comment: A residential development SCM with water quality volume exceeding 5,000 cubic feet requires a labeled maintenance access drive with a minimum 14-foot vertical clearance from all existing and proposed vegetation and other objects. The plans do not identify, delineate, or dimension a maintenance access drive meeting these requirements, nor do they demonstrate the required 14-foot clearance at maturity of vegetation.

applicableAreas: All areas with overhead electric distribution lines (southern property boundary and southeastern corner per Sheets 21 and 9); entire site for transmission clearance envelope if applicable
findings.comment: Site and utility plans show existing overhead electric (OHE) lines but do not graphically delineate the required distribution clearance envelopes: a 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance boundary measured from the outermost conductor, and a 15-foot radial clearance zone from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Additionally, no transmission clearance envelope analysis or graphic delineation from Austin Energy is included on the plans.

applicableAreas: Site plan and utility plan sheets showing overhead electric lines
findings.comment: Site plan (Sheet 9) and utility plan (Sheet 21) do not include horizontal dashed height limit lines to delineate the overhead electric conductor clearance envelope boundaries where overhead utility hazards are present.

applicableAreas: Site plan and grading plan areas with non-uniform (sloped) terrain beneath overhead utilities
findings.comment: Grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9) show variable site elevations (ranging from approximately 672 feet to 687 feet MSL) beneath existing overhead electric facilities, requiring sloped or stepped dashed height limit lines to reflect actual grade changes under the overhead conductor span. These are not shown on any plans.
